title.zh: 卷九十二 列傳第五十二 良吏
title.raw: 卷九十二 列傳第五十二 良吏 Volume 92 Biographies 52: Liang Li

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十二 良吏

translations.literal: Biography 52: Good Officials
translations.idiomatic: Biography 52: Good Magistrates

sentences.zh: 高祖起自匹庶，知民事艱難，及登庸作宰，留心吏職，而王略外舉，未遑內務。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor rose from commoner rank, knew the hardship of the people's affairs; when he ascended the throne and became chief minister, he paid attention to officials' duties, but royal strategy looked outward and he had no leisure for internal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu rose from humble origins and understood how hard life was for ordinary people. Once he took power as chief minister, he kept a close eye on local administration, but with his grand strategy focused abroad he had little time for domestic governance.

sentences.zh: 奉師之費，日耗千金，播茲寬簡，雖所未暇，而絀華屏欲，以儉抑身，左右無幸謁之私，閨房無文綺之飾，故能戎車歲駕，邦甸不憂。

translations.literal: The cost of maintaining the army consumed a thousand gold daily; to spread such leniency and simplicity he had no leisure, yet he reined in splendor and barred indulgence, restraining himself through frugality; those at his side had no privilege of private audiences, inner chambers had no brocade ornaments; therefore the war chariot could set out year after year yet the realm was not troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Army expenses ran to a thousand gold a day, and he had not yet found time to carry out the full program of leniency and simplicity he envisioned; still he cut back display, checked his desires, and practiced austerity in his own life. No favorite at court enjoyed private access, and his inner quarters held no silk brocade. Thus he could campaign every year without overwhelming the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖幼而寬仁，入纂大業，及難興陝方，六戎薄伐，命將動師，經略司、兗，費由府實，役不及民。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was from youth broad and benevolent; he entered to succeed the great enterprise; when trouble arose in the Shaan region and the six Rong pressed in attack, he ordered generals to move troops, planning strategy in Si and Yan provinces; expenses came from the treasury stores and corvée labor did not reach the people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was gentle and magnanimous from childhood. When he inherited the throne and trouble flared in the northwest, with the northern peoples pressing south, he sent generals to campaign in the Si and Yan regions, paying for it all from the state treasury so that the burden did not fall on the common people.

sentences.zh: 自此區宇宴安，方內無事，三十年間，氓庶蕃息，奉上供徭，止於歲賦，晨出莫歸，自事而已。

translations.literal: From this the realm was tranquil and secure, within the four quarters there was no trouble; for thirty years the common people multiplied; what they offered to the state in labor and levies stopped at the annual tax; they went out at dawn and returned at dusk, attending only to their own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the empire enjoyed peace and the heartland knew no unrest. For thirty years the population grew; what the people owed the state was limited to the annual land tax. They left at dawn and came home at dusk, minding only their own work.

sentences.zh: 守宰之職，以六期為斷，雖沒世不徙，未及曩時，而民有所係，吏無苟得。

translations.literal: The office of prefect and magistrate was fixed at six-year terms; although one might serve until death without transfer, it did not match former times, yet the people had someone to rely on and officials could not grab gains at will.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates served fixed six-year terms. Though an appointee might hold a post for life without transfer, this fell short of earlier practice; still the people had officials they could depend on, and magistrates could not seize profit as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 家給人足，即事雖難，轉死溝渠，于時可免。

translations.literal: Households had enough and people were provided for; even when affairs were difficult, dying abandoned in ditches and drains could at that time be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Households were supplied and people had enough to live on; even when times were hard, the fate of starving by the roadside could, in that age, largely be avoided.

sentences.zh: 凡百戶之鄉，有市之邑，歌謠舞蹈，觸處成群，蓋宋世之極盛也。

translations.literal: In every village of a hundred households, in every market town, songs and dances—wherever one touched, they gathered in groups; this was roughly the greatest flourishing of the Song age.
translations.idiomatic: In hamlets of a hundred households and in market towns alike, people sang and danced; crowds formed wherever one went. This was the Song dynasty at its height.

sentences.zh: 暨元嘉二十七年，北狄南侵，戎役大起，傾資掃蓄，猶有未供，於是深賦厚斂，天下騷動。

translations.literal: When the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia arrived, northern barbarians invaded south; military service rose greatly; pouring out funds and sweeping away savings still could not meet demand; then deep taxes and heavy levies were imposed and the realm was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia (450), the northern peoples invaded the south. Military levies surged; families spent their savings to the last coin and still could not meet the demand. Heavy taxes followed, and the whole empire was thrown into unrest.

sentences.zh: 自茲至於孝建，兵連不息，以區區之江東，地方不至數千里，戶不盈百萬，薦之以師旅，因之以凶荒，宋氏之盛，自此衰矣。

translations.literal: From this until Xiaojian, warfare continued without cease; with the mere Jiangdong region, territory not reaching several thousand li, households not filling a million—add military expeditions on top, follow with famine and disaster—the flourishing of the Song house from this declined.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the Xiaojian era (454–456), war never ceased. The southeast alone, a territory of less than a few thousand li and fewer than a million households, was burdened with armies and then struck by famine. The Song dynasty's prosperity waned from that point.

sentences.zh: 晉世諸帝，多處內房，朝宴所臨，東西二堂而已。

translations.literal: The emperors of the Jin age mostly dwelt in inner chambers; for morning audiences and banquets they attended only the Eastern and Western halls.
translations.idiomatic: Jin emperors mostly lived within the inner palace; court audiences and banquets were held in only the Eastern and Western halls.

sentences.zh: 孝武末年，清暑方構，高祖受命，無所改作，所居唯稱西殿，不制嘉名；

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu, the Clear Summer Palace was just being built; when the Founder Emperor received the Mandate he made no alterations, calling his residence only the Western Hall and giving it no fine name;
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Clear Summer Palace was under construction. When Gaozu took the throne he changed nothing, calling his residence simply the Western Hall and giving it no grand title;

sentences.zh: 太祖因之，亦有合殿之稱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen followed this, and there was also the name Combined Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen followed his example, and the hall was also called the Combined Hall.

sentences.zh: 及世祖承統，制度奢廣，犬馬餘菽粟，土木衣綈繡，追陋前規，更造正光、玉燭、紫極諸殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the succession, institutions were extravagant and broad; dogs and horses had surplus grain and millet, earth and wood wore silk gauze and brocade; pursuing what he deemed shabby in former rules, he newly built the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, luxury spread through the court. Horses and dogs had grain to spare while palaces were draped in silk; deeming earlier standards mean, he built anew the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls.

sentences.zh: 雕欒綺節，珠窗網戶，嬖女幸臣，賜傾府藏，竭四海不供其欲，單民命未快其心。

translations.literal: Carved beams with brocade ornament, pearl windows and latticed doors; favored women and trusted ministers received gifts that emptied the treasury; exhausting the four seas could not supply their desires, and the lives of common people could not satisfy their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Carved beams bore brocade ornament; pearl windows and latticed doors adorned the halls. Favorites and trusted ministers received gifts that drained the treasury; the wealth of the entire realm could not satisfy their appetites, and the common people's very lives could not content them.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼阼，彌篤浮侈，恩不恤下，以至橫流。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne, even more devoted to frivolity and extravagance, grace not caring for those below, until it reached flood tide.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded him, extravagance grew worse still. Favor no longer reached those below, and disorder spread like a flood.

sentences.zh: 蒞民之官，遷變歲屬，灶不得黔，席未暇暖，蒲、密之化，事未易階。

translations.literal: Officials who governed the people changed with each year's turn; the stove could not be blackened, the mat had no time to grow warm—the transformation of Pu and Mi was not easily attained.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who governed the people were rotated every year; their stoves never blackened and their mats never grew warm. The gentle governance once seen under officials such as Pu and Mi could no longer be achieved.

sentences.zh: 豈徒吏不及古，民偽于昔，蓋由為上所擾，致治莫從。

translations.literal: Was it only that officials did not match antiquity and the people were false compared with the past? It was fundamentally because they were disturbed by those above, so that achieving good government had no path to follow.
translations.idiomatic: It was not merely that officials fell short of those of old or that the people had grown deceitful. The court itself disrupted governance, leaving no way to restore order.

sentences.zh: 今采其風跡粗著者，以為《良吏篇》云。

translations.literal: Now I gather those whose conduct and traces are roughly notable, to make the 'Good Officials' chapter.
translations.idiomatic: I now select those whose reputations stand out clearly enough to compose this chapter on good magistrates.

sentences.zh: 王鎮之，字伯重，琅邪臨沂人，征士弘之兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenzhi, styled Bozhong, was a man of Linyi in Langye, elder brother of the recluse Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi, courtesy name Bozhong, was from Linyi in Langye and elder brother of the recluse Wang Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖廙，晉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was Jin General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wang Yi served as Jin General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 祖耆之，中書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Qizhi was a Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父隨之，上虞令。

translations.literal: His father Suizhi was magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Suizhi was magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 鎮之初為琅邪王衛軍行參軍，出補剡、上虞令，並有能名。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi at first was Acting Adjutant in the Guard Army of the Prince of Langye; he went out to fill posts as magistrate of Shan and Shangyu, in both gaining a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi first served as acting adjutant in the guard army of the Prince of Langye, then was appointed magistrate of Shan and Shangyu in succession, earning a name for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 內史謝輶請為山陰令，復有殊績。

translations.literal: Interior Secretary Xie Zhou requested him as magistrate of Shanyin; again he had outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Secretary Xie Zhou requested him as magistrate of Shanyin, where he again achieved exceptional results.

sentences.zh: 遷衛軍參軍，本國郎中令，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Adjutant in the Guard Army, Grandee Master of the original state, with additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to adjutant in the guard army and grandee master of his native principality, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，以為大將軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, he was made Recorder of the Grand General's Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan controlled the Jin court, Zhenzhi was appointed recorder of the grand general's affairs.

sentences.zh: 時三吳饑荒，遣鎮之銜命賑恤，而會稽內史王愉不奉符旨，鎮之依事糾奏。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Wu regions suffered famine; Zhenzhi was sent bearing orders to relieve and succor; but Interior Secretary of Kuaiji Wang Yu did not follow the written command, and Zhenzhi impeached him according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Three Wu region, Zhenzhi was dispatched on imperial orders to provide relief. Wang Yu, interior secretary of Kuaiji, refused to carry out the directive, and Zhenzhi impeached him on the facts.

sentences.zh: 愉子綏，玄之外甥，當時貴盛，鎮之為所排抑，以母老求補安成太守。

translations.literal: Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew by marriage and at the time noble and powerful; Zhenzhi was suppressed by them and, citing his mother's age, requested appointment as Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew by marriage and immensely powerful at court. Zhenzhi was forced out and, pleading his mother's advanced age, asked to be appointed administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 及玄敗，玄將苻宏寇亂郡境，鎮之拒戰彌年，子弟五人，並臨陣見殺。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated, Xuan's general Fu Hong raided and disturbed the commandery borders; Zhenzhi resisted in battle for a full year; five sons and younger brothers were all killed facing the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's fall, his general Fu Hong raided the commandery. Zhenzhi held out for a full year; five of his sons and younger brothers were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，在官清潔，妻子無以自給，乃棄家致喪還上虞舊基。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office; while in office he had been pure and clean, wife and children had no means to support themselves, so he abandoned his household and conveyed the coffin back to his old home base in Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. His official service had been so incorrupt that his wife and children could not support themselves; he gave up his household goods and brought her coffin back to his family home in Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 畢，為子標之求安復令，隨子之官。

translations.literal: When the mourning was complete, he sought for his son Biaozhi the post of magistrate of Anfu and followed his son to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he secured for his son Biaozhi the post of magistrate of Anfu and went with him to take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為征西道規司馬、南平太守。

translations.literal: When mourning was over, he became Marshal of the Western Expeditionary Army under Dao Gui and Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as marshal on Liu Daogui's western campaign staff and as administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆逼江陵，加鎮之建威將軍，統檀道濟、到彥之等討道覆，以不經將帥，固辭，不見聽。

translations.literal: When Xu Daofu pressed Jiangling, Zhenzhi was given additional title General Who Establishes Might and commanded Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and others to attack Daofu; because he had not passed through the ranks of commanders, he firmly declined and was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Daofu threatened Jiangling, Zhenzhi was made General Who Establishes Might and placed over Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and others to suppress him. He declined firmly on the ground that he had never held field command, but his protest was ignored.

sentences.zh: 既而前軍失利，白衣領職，尋復本官。

translations.literal: Soon after the vanguard army was defeated; he held office in plain dress; shortly he was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard was soon defeated, and he was reduced to commoner's dress while retaining his post; shortly afterward he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 以討道覆功，封華容縣五等男，徵廷尉。

translations.literal: For merit in attacking Daofu, he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Baron of Huarong and summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For his service against Xu Daofu he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Baron of Huarong and summoned to the post of Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝何皇后山陵，領將作大匠。

translations.literal: For the mountain tomb of Empress He of Emperor Mudi of Jin, he concurrently held the post of Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction of the tomb of Empress He, consort of Emperor Mudi of Jin, serving concurrently as Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，秉正不撓，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor; upright and unbending, the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Imperial Censor, where his upright and unyielding conduct made the entire bureaucracy fear him.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、都督交、廣二州諸軍事、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander over military affairs of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, area commander of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂人曰：「王鎮之少著清績，必將繼美吳隱之。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor said to others: "Wang Zhenzhi from youth has shown a record of purity; he will surely continue the fine reputation of Wu Yinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told his court: "Wang Zhenzhi has been known for integrity since his youth; he will surely follow in the footsteps of Wu Yinshi.

sentences.zh: 嶺南之弊，非此不康也。」

translations.literal: The ills of Lingnan, without this man, will not be made secure."
translations.idiomatic: The troubles of the far south cannot be remedied without a man like him."

sentences.zh: 在鎮不受俸祿，蕭然無所營。

translations.literal: In his post he did not accept salary, desolate and with nothing he pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In his post he refused his salary and lived in austere simplicity, pursuing no private gain.

sentences.zh: 去官之日，不異始至。

translations.literal: On the day he left office, he was no different from when he first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he was no richer than the day he had arrived.

sentences.zh: 高祖初建相國府，以為諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor first established the Chancellor's Office, he was made Consulting Adjutant and concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first established his chancellor's office, Zhenzhi was made consulting adjutant and chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 善於吏職，嚴而不殘。

translations.literal: He was skilled in official duties, strict but not cruel.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at administrative work, strict but never cruel.

sentences.zh: 遷宋臺祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites of the Song Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites of the Song regime.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，鎮之以腳患自陳，出為輔國將軍、琅邪太守，遷宣訓衛尉，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Zhenzhi reported himself on account of foot ailment; he went out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Langye, was transferred to Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard, and concurrently held Grand Rectifier of the original province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Zhenzhi cited a foot ailment and left the capital to serve as General Who Assists the State and administrator of Langye, then became commandant of the Xuanxun guard and grand rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，卒官，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died in office, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu (422) he died in office at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 弟弘之，在《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hongzhi is in the 'Recluses' biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hongzhi is treated in the chapter on recluses.

sentences.zh: 杜慧度，交趾朱鸘人也。

translations.literal: Du Huidu was a man of Zhuying in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu was from Zhuying in Jiaozhi commandery.

sentences.zh: 本屬京兆。

translations.literal: His clan originally belonged to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was originally registered in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元，為寧浦太守，遂居交趾。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuan was Administrator of Ningpu and thereafter settled in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Du Yuan served as administrator of Ningpu and then settled in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 父瑗，字道言，仕州府為日南、九德、交趾太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuan, styled Daoyan, served the provincial administration as Administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi in turn.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Yuan, courtesy name Daoyan, served the province as administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi in succession.

sentences.zh: 初，九真太守李遜父子勇壯有權力，威制交土，聞刺史騰遯之當至，分遣二子斷遏水陸津要。

translations.literal: At first Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, father and sons, were brave and strong with power, dominating Jiaozhi by might; hearing that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was about to arrive, they separately sent two sons to block and hold the water and land passes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Xun, administrator of Jiuzhen, and his sons were powerful local strongmen who dominated the region. Learning that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was on his way, they sent two sons to seize the strategic passes by land and water.

sentences.zh: 瑗收眾斬遜，州境獲寧。

translations.literal: Yuan gathered troops and beheaded Xun; the province's territory was secured in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan raised troops, killed Li Xun, and restored peace to the province.

sentences.zh: 除龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遯之在州十餘年，與林邑累相攻伐。

translations.literal: Dunzhi was in the province more than ten years and with Linyi repeatedly attacked and fought each other.
translations.idiomatic: Dunzhi spent more than ten years in the province, fighting repeated campaigns against Linyi.

sentences.zh: 遯之將北還，林邑王范胡達攻破日南、九德、九真三郡，遂圍州城。

translations.literal: When Dunzhi was about to return north, the King of Linyi Fan Huda broke through the three commanderies Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen, and then besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Dunzhi prepared to return north, the king of Linyi, Fan Huda, overran Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen and besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 時遯之去已遠，瑗與第三子玄之悉力固守，多設權策，累戰，大破之。

translations.literal: At that time Dunzhi had already gone far; Yuan and his third son Xuanzhi exerted all strength to defend firmly, set many stratagems, fought repeatedly, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Dunzhi was already far away. Yuan and his third son Xuanzhi defended the city with all their strength, using many stratagems through repeated battles until they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 追討於九真、日南。

translations.literal: They pursued and attacked in Jiuzhen and Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the enemy into Jiuzhen and Rinan.

sentences.zh: 連捷，故胡達走還林邑。

translations.literal: Victories followed in succession, so Huda fled back to Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Victory followed victory until Fan Huda fled back to Linyi.

sentences.zh: 乃以瑗為龍驤將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was made General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was then appointed General of Agile Cavalry and inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 義旗進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Banner of Righteousness rose, his title was advanced to General Who Conquers.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised the banner of righteous restoration, Yuan was promoted to General Who Conquers.

sentences.zh: 盧循竊據廣州，遣使通好，瑗斬之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun seized and held Guangzhou and sent envoys to seek friendship; Yuan beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun had seized Guangzhou and sent envoys offering alliance; Yuan had them executed.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年，年八十四，卒，追贈右將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yixi, age eighty-four, he died; posthumously he was given the Right General, his original office unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yixi (410), at the age of eighty-four, he died and was posthumously made Right General with his former titles confirmed.

sentences.zh: 慧度，瑗第五子也。

translations.literal: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初為州主簿，流民督護，遷九真太守。

translations.literal: At first he was provincial Registrar, Protector of Displaced Persons, and was transferred to Administrator of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He began as provincial registrar and protector of displaced persons, then was promoted to administrator of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 瑗卒，府州綱佐以交土接寇，不宜曠職，共推慧度行州府事，辭不就。

translations.literal: When Yuan died, the leading aides of the prefecture and province, because Jiaozhi bordered raiders and the post should not be left vacant, jointly urged Huidu to conduct provincial affairs; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, provincial officials urged Huidu to take charge, arguing that with enemies on the border the post could not remain empty. He declined.

sentences.zh: 七年，除使持節、督交州諸軍事、廣武將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over military affairs of Jiaozhou, General of Expansive Might, and Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi (411) he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, commander of Jiaozhou military affairs, General of Expansive Might, and inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔書未至，其年春，盧循襲破合浦，徑向交州。

translations.literal: Before the imperial edict arrived, that spring Lu Xun raided and broke Hepu, heading straight for Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial appointment arrived, that spring Lu Xun overran Hepu and marched directly on Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 慧度乃率文武六千人距循於石碕，交戰，禽循長史孫建之。

translations.literal: Huidu then led six thousand civil and military men to resist Xun at Shiji, joined battle, and captured Xun's Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu led six thousand troops to meet Lu Xun at Shiji, fought a battle, and captured Xun's chief clerk Sun Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 循雖敗，餘黨猶有三千人，皆習練兵事。

translations.literal: Although Xun was defeated, his remaining followers still numbered three thousand, all practiced and trained in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though defeated, Lu Xun still had three thousand seasoned fighters among his remnants.

sentences.zh: 李子遜李弈、李脫等奔竄石碕，盤結俚、獠，各有部曲。

translations.literal: Li Zixun, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others fled and scattered at Shiji, entrenched with Li and Liao peoples, each with his own following.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixun, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others had fled to Shiji, where they allied with local Li and Liao chiefs, each commanding his own band.

sentences.zh: 循知弈等與杜氏有怨，遣使招之，弈等引諸俚帥眾五六千人，受循節度。

translations.literal: Xun knew that Yi and others bore a grudge against the Du clan; he sent envoys to recruit them; Yi and others led the various Li chiefs with forces of five or six thousand and accepted Xun's command.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Li Yi and his brothers bore a grudge against the Du family, Lu Xun sent envoys to win them over. They brought five or six thousand Li warriors under his command.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，循晨造南津，命三軍入城乃食。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month, Xun at dawn reached the Southern Ford and ordered the three armies to enter the city before eating.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month, Lu Xun reached the southern ford at dawn and ordered his three armies not to eat until they had entered the city.

sentences.zh: 慧度悉出宗族私財，以充勸賞。

translations.literal: Huidu brought out all his clan's private wealth to supply rewards and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu spent his entire clan's private fortune to pay battle rewards.

sentences.zh: 弟交趾太守慧期、九真太守章民並督率水步軍，慧度自登高艦，合戰，放火箭雉尾炬，步軍夾兩岸射之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huiqi, Administrator of Jiaozhi, and Zhang Min, Administrator of Jiuzhen, both commanded water and land forces; Huidu himself boarded a tall warship; they joined battle, loosing fire arrows and pheasant-tail torches, while infantry on both banks shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huiqi, administrator of Jiaozhi, and Zhang Min, administrator of Jiuzhen, commanded the land and naval forces while Huidu took a tall warship into the fight. They loosed fire arrows and pheasant-tail torches while infantry on both banks rained arrows on the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 循眾艦俱然，一時散潰，循中箭赴水死。

translations.literal: All of Xun's ships caught fire together; in a moment they scattered and collapsed; Xun was struck by an arrow, went into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's entire fleet burst into flame and broke apart. Lu Xun was struck by an arrow, fell into the water, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 斬循及父嘏，並循二子，親屬錄事參軍阮靜、中兵參軍羅農夫、李脫等，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: They beheaded Xun and his father Gu, together with Xun's two sons, and kinsmen Recorder Sun Jing, Central Army Adjutant Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others; their heads were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded Lu Xun, his father Gu, and his two sons, along with his kinsmen Sun Jing, Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others, and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 封慧度龍編縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Huidu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longbian with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longbian with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Huidu's title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Huidu was promoted to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，率文武萬人南討林邑，所殺過半，前後被抄略，悉得還本。

translations.literal: That year he led ten thousand civil and military men south to attack Linyi; more than half were killed; those who had earlier been raided and carried off all were returned to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he led ten thousand troops south against Linyi, killing more than half the enemy force and recovering all the people who had been carried off in earlier raids.

sentences.zh: 林邑乞降，輸生口、大象、金銀、古貝等，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Linyi begged to surrender, presenting captives, elephants, gold and silver, ancient cowries, and the like; he then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi sued for peace, offering captives, elephants, gold, silver, and cowrie shells, and Huidu accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 遣長史江悠奉表獻捷。

translations.literal: He sent Chief Clerk Jiang You to present a memorial reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his chief clerk Jiang You to the capital with a report of victory.

sentences.zh: 慧度布衣蔬食，儉約質素，能彈琴，頗好《莊》、《老》。

translations.literal: Huidu wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, was frugal and simple in substance, could play the zither, and rather favored the Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu dressed in plain cloth and ate simple fare, living frugally and without pretension. He played the zither and was fond of the Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祀，崇脩學校。

translations.literal: He forbade and cut off improper sacrifices and honored and repaired schools.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed illicit cults and promoted the schools.

sentences.zh: 歲荒民饑，則以私祿賑給。

translations.literal: When the year was barren and the people hungry, he used his private salary to relieve and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he used his private salary to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 為政纖密，有如治家，由是威惠沾洽，姦盜不起，乃至城門不夜閉，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: In governing he was meticulous, as if managing a household; thereby authority and kindness permeated, treachery and theft did not arise, until city gates were not closed at night and lost things were not picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with the meticulous care of a household manager, so that his authority and kindness reached everyone. Crime vanished; city gates stood open at night and no one picked up lost goods on the road.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平元年，卒，時年五十，追贈左將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping under Emperor Shao, he died, age fifty; posthumously he was given the Left General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping (423), under Emperor Shao, he died at the age of fifty and was posthumously made Left General.

sentences.zh: 以慧度長子員外散騎侍郎弘文為振威將軍、刺史。

translations.literal: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat Outside the Palace, was made General Who Quells Might and Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, an attendant gentleman at the Secretariat, was appointed General Who Quells Might and inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖北征關、洛，慧度板弘文為鷹揚將軍，流民督護，配兵三千，北係大軍。

translations.literal: At first, when the Founder Emperor campaigned north to Guan and Luo, Huidu commissioned Hongwen as General of Soaring Valor, Protector of Displaced Persons, with three thousand troops assigned, to join the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, Huidu commissioned Hongwen as General of Soaring Valor and protector of displaced persons, assigning him three thousand men to join the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 行至廣州，關、洛已平，乃歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangzhou, Guan and Luo had already been pacified, so he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Guangzhou only to learn that Guanzhong and Luoyang had already been pacified, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 統府板弘文行九真太守。

translations.literal: The area headquarters commissioned Hongwen to act as Administrator of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial headquarters appointed him acting administrator of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 及繼父為刺史，亦以寬和得眾，襲爵龍編侯。

translations.literal: When he succeeded his father as Inspector, he also won the people through leniency and harmony, and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded his father as inspector, he too won the people's loyalty through leniency and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉四年，以廷尉王徽為交州刺史，弘文就徴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Wang Hui the Minister of Justice was made Inspector of Jiaozhou, and Hongwen was summoned to yield the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia (427), Emperor Wen appointed Wang Hui, Minister of Justice, as inspector of Jiaozhou, and Hongwen was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會得重疾，牽以就路，親舊見其患篤，勸表待病癒。

translations.literal: He happened to contract a severe illness but was dragged along on the journey; relatives and friends seeing his illness grave urged him to memorialize and wait until the illness healed.
translations.idiomatic: He fell gravely ill but was compelled to set out anyway. Friends and relatives, seeing how serious his condition was, urged him to petition the throne for leave to recover first.

sentences.zh: 弘文曰：「吾世荷皇恩，杖節三世，常欲投軀帝庭，以報所荷。

translations.literal: Hongwen said: "Our family for generations has borne the imperial grace; bearing the staff of authority for three generations, I have always wished to cast my body before the imperial court to repay what I have borne.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen said: "Our family has borne the imperial favor for generations. For three generations we have held the staff of authority, and I have long wished to give my life at court in repayment.

sentences.zh: 況親被徵命，而可宴然者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when I have personally received a summons—can I remain at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have been personally summoned, how can I remain at ease?

sentences.zh: 如其顛沛，此乃命也。」

translations.literal: If I should suffer hardship and ruin, that is fate."
translations.idiomatic: If hardship should overtake me on the road, that is fate."

sentences.zh: 弘文母既年老，見弘文輿疾就路，不忍分別，相與俱行。

translations.literal: Hongwen's mother was already old; seeing Hongwen take to his carriage ill and set out on the road, she could not bear to part and traveled together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen's mother was elderly. Seeing her son set out in a sickbed carriage, she could not bear to part from him and traveled with him.

sentences.zh: 到廣州，遂卒。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangzhou, he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Guangzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 臨死，遣弟弘猷詣京，朝廷甚哀之。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he sent his younger brother Hongyou to the capital; the court greatly mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died he sent his younger brother Hongyou to the capital; the court mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 徐豁，字萬同，東莞姑幕人也，中散大夫廣兄子。

translations.literal: Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan, nephew of Palace Attendant Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huo, courtesy name Wantong, was from Gumu in Dongguan and nephew of Palace Attendant Xu Guang.

sentences.zh: 父邈，晉太子左衛率。

translations.literal: His father Miao was Jin Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Miao was left commandant of the crown prince's guard under Jin.

sentences.zh: 豁晉安帝隆安末為太學博士。

translations.literal: Huo at the end of Longan under Emperor An of Jin was Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Longan era under Emperor An of Jin, Huo served as erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，為中外都督，豁議：「致敬唯內外武官，太宰、司徒，並非軍職，則琅邪王不應加敬。」

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted in government as Area Commander of Inner and Outer Affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect is only for inner and outer military officials; the Grand Tutor and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not be given added respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held power as area commander of inner and outer affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect applies only to military officials. The Grand Tutor and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not receive added obeisance.

sentences.zh: 玄諷中丞免豁官。

translations.literal: Xuan prompted the Imperial Censor to dismiss Huo from office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan prompted the imperial censor to have Huo removed from office.

sentences.zh: 玄敗，以為秘書郎，尚書倉部郎，右軍何無忌功曹，仍為鎮南參軍；

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated, he was made Secretariat Gentleman, Gentleman of the Granaries Section in the Secretariat, Merit Officer under He Wuji of the Right Army, and then Adjutant of the Army Pacifying the South;
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's defeat, Huo served as secretariat gentleman, gentleman of the granaries section, merit officer under He Wuji of the right army, and then adjutant of the army pacifying the south;

sentences.zh: 又祠部，永世令，建武司馬，中軍參軍，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: also in the Rites Section, Magistrate of Yongshi, Marshal of the Army Establishing Might, Adjutant in the Central Army, and Left Assistant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: then in the rites section, magistrate of Yongshi, marshal of the army establishing might, adjutant in the central army, and left assistant in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永初初，為徐羨之鎮軍司馬，尚書左丞，山陰令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu he was Marshal of the Pacifying Army under Xu Xianzhi, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, and Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongchu he served as marshal of the pacifying army under Xu Xianzhi, left assistant in the secretariat, and magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 歷二丞三邑，精練明理，為一世所推。

translations.literal: Having passed through two assistant posts and three districts, he was skilled and clear in principle and was esteemed by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Having served as two assistant ministers and three district magistrates, he was known for mastery of law and administration and was highly regarded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為始興太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was appointed administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣大使巡行四方，並使郡縣各言損益。

translations.literal: In the third year envoys were sent to tour the four quarters, and prefectures and counties were also ordered each to speak of what should be reduced or increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the throne sent envoys to tour the realm and ordered every prefecture and county to report what policies should be changed.

sentences.zh: 豁因此表陳三事，其一曰：「郡大田，武吏年滿十六，便課米六十斛，十五以下至十三，皆課米三十斛，一戶內隨丁多少，悉皆輸米。

translations.literal: Huo therefore memorialized setting forth three matters. The first said: "In the commandery's great fields, when a military household's male reaches sixteen, he is levied sixty hu of grain; from fifteen down to thirteen, each is levied thirty hu; within a household, according to how many males there are, all must deliver grain.
translations.idiomatic: Huo submitted a memorial on three matters. The first read: "In this commandery's land-tax system, when a military household's son turns sixteen he is assessed sixty hu of grain; from fifteen down to thirteen the assessment is thirty hu each. Every household must pay according to the number of males, with all grain delivered in kind.

sentences.zh: 且十三歲兒，未堪田作，或是單迥，無相兼通，年及應輸，便自逃逸，既遏接蠻、俚，去就益易。

translations.literal: Moreover a boy of thirteen is not yet able for field work, or is a lone household with no one to share the burden; when the year comes that he should pay, he flees on his own; since this borders on Man and Li peoples, coming and going is all the easier.
translations.idiomatic: A boy of thirteen cannot yet work the fields; some households have only one son and no one to share the burden. When the levy comes due they flee. With barbarian and Li territory nearby, flight is easy.

sentences.zh: 或乃斷截支體，產子不養，戶口歲減，實此之由。

translations.literal: Some even cut off limbs or bear children and do not rear them; registered population diminishes year by year—this is truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Some mutilate their children or abandon newborns. The registered population shrinks every year, and this policy is the reason.

sentences.zh: 謂宜更量課限，使得存立。

translations.literal: I hold that the levy limits should be reconsidered so that people can survive and stand.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the levy thresholds be revised so that families can survive.

sentences.zh: 今若減其米課，雖有交損，考之將來，理有深益。」

translations.literal: If the grain levy is now reduced, although there will be mutual loss in the short term, considering the future, in principle there is deep benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing the grain levy would cause a short-term loss of revenue, but in the long run the benefit would be great.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：「郡領銀民三百餘戶，鑿坑采砂，皆二三丈。

translations.literal: The second said: "The commandery oversees more than three hundred silver-mining households; they dig pits to extract ore, all two or three zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: The second matter: "More than three hundred households in this commandery mine silver, digging pits two or three zhang deep to extract ore.

sentences.zh: 功役既苦，不顧崩壓，一歲之中，每有死者。

translations.literal: The labor service is bitter; they do not heed cave-ins and crushing; within a year there are deaths every so often.
translations.idiomatic: The work is brutal; miners ignore the risk of collapse, and deaths occur throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 官司檢切，猶致逋違，老少相隨，永絕農業；

translations.literal: Though the authorities press and scrutinize, they still fall into default; old and young follow one another, forever cut off from agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: Despite official pressure, many still default on the levy. Whole families, young and old together, abandon farming forever;

sentences.zh: 千有餘口，皆資他食，豈唯一夫不耕，或受其饑而已。

translations.literal: more than a thousand mouths all rely on others' food—how could it be only that one man does not plow and someone suffers hunger?
translations.idiomatic: more than a thousand people depend on others for food. The harm is not merely that one man leaves the plow and goes hungry.

sentences.zh: 所以歲有不稔，便致甚困。

translations.literal: Therefore when a year is not abundant, extreme hardship follows at once.
translations.idiomatic: That is why a single bad harvest brings extreme distress.

sentences.zh: 尋臺邸用米，不異於銀，謂宜准銀課米，即事為便。」

translations.literal: Considering that the metropolitan offices use grain no differently from silver, I hold that silver levies should be converted to grain levies on the same basis—this would be convenient in practice.
translations.idiomatic: The central government uses grain no less than silver. I propose converting the silver levy to a grain levy, which would be far more practical.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：「中宿縣俚民課銀，一子丁輸南稱半兩。

translations.literal: The third said: "In Zhongsu County the Li people are levied silver; each adult male delivers half a liang by the southern weight.
translations.idiomatic: The third matter: "In Zhongsu County the Li people are assessed silver at half a liang per adult male by the southern weight.

sentences.zh: 尋此縣自不出銀，又俚民皆巢居鳥語，不閑貨易之宜，每至買銀，為損已甚。

translations.literal: Considering that this county itself produces no silver, and the Li all dwell in nests and speak bird languages, unskilled in the proprieties of trade—each time they must buy silver the loss to them is very great.
translations.idiomatic: This county produces no silver. The Li live in tree houses and speak their own languages; they know nothing of commerce. Every time they must buy silver to pay the tax the loss to them is severe.

sentences.zh: 又稱兩受入，易生姦巧，山俚愚怯，不辨自申，官所課甚輕，民以所輸為劇。

translations.literal: Moreover with weighing by the liang at collection, fraud and trickery easily arise; mountain Li are foolish and timid and cannot plead for themselves; what the government levies is very light, yet the people find what they must deliver oppressive.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing at collection invites fraud. The mountain Li are simple and timid and cannot plead their case. The official levy is light on paper, yet what the people actually pay is crushing.

sentences.zh: 今若聽計丁課米，公私兼利。」

translations.literal: If they are now allowed to pay grain assessed per male, both public and private will benefit together."
translations.idiomatic: If they were allowed to pay grain per male instead, both state and people would benefit."

sentences.zh: 在郡著績，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the commandery he achieved notable results; Emperor Wen commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He achieved notable results in the commandery, and Emperor Wen praised him.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「始興太守豁，潔己退食，恪居在官，政事脩理，惠澤沾被。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Administrator of Shixing Huo, pure in himself and frugal in eating, reverent in holding office, government affairs well ordered, favor and grace spreading over all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Xu Huo, administrator of Shixing, is frugal and self-restrained, diligent in office, orderly in administration, and generous in his care for the people.

sentences.zh: 近嶺南荒弊，郡境尤甚，拯恤有方，濟厥饑饉，雖古之良守，蔑以尚焉。

translations.literal: Recently Lingnan has been desolate and impoverished, and his commandery's territory is especially so; he has had methods to rescue and succor, relieving their famine—even good magistrates of antiquity could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan has lately been destitute, and his commandery especially so; yet he found effective means to relieve famine. Even the best magistrates of antiquity could not surpass him.

sentences.zh: 宜蒙褒賁，以旌清績，可賜絹二百匹，穀千斛。」

translations.literal: He should receive praise and reward to display his pure achievements; he may be granted two hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He deserves reward to honor his integrity: grant him two hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 五年，以為持節、督廣、交二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Guang and Jiao provinces, General of Tranquil Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed bearer of the staff, commander of Guang and Jiao military affairs, General of Tranquil Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the post he died, age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment he died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 太祖又下詔曰：「豁廉清勤恪，著稱所司，故擢授南服，申其才志。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again issued an edict: "Huo was pure, clean, diligent, and reverent, renowned in the office he served; therefore he was promoted and sent to the southern regions to give scope to his talent and will.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen issued another edict: "Huo was known for integrity and diligence in every post he held. We promoted him to the south to give full scope to his abilities.

sentences.zh: 不幸喪殞，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: Unhappily he died; We deeply mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: He has died untimely, and We deeply mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可賜錢十萬，布百匹，以營葬事。」

translations.literal: He may be granted a hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth for funeral arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him a hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral."

sentences.zh: 陸徽，字休猷，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Hui, styled Xiuyou, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui, courtesy name Xiuyou, was from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡辟命主簿，仍除衛軍、車騎二府參軍，揚州主簿，王弘衛將軍主簿，除尚書都官郎，出補建康令。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as Registrar; he was then appointed Adjutant in the Guard Army and Cavalry General's offices, Registrar of Yangzhou, Registrar under Wang Hong the General of the Guard, made Gentleman of the Punishments Section in the Secretariat, and went out to fill the post of Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery summoned him as registrar. He then served as adjutant in the guard army and cavalry general's offices, as registrar of Yangzhou and registrar under Wang Hong, as gentleman of the punishments section, and finally as magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 清平無私，為太祖所善，遷司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Pure, fair, and without private bias, he was favored by Emperor Wen and was transferred to Left Western Attendant of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, impartial, and incorrupt, he won Emperor Wen's favor and was promoted to left western attendant of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十四年，為始興太守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia he was Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia he was appointed administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 明年，仍除使持節、交、廣二州諸軍事、綏遠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over military affairs of Jiao and Guang provinces, General of Pacifying Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, commander of Jiao and Guang military affairs, General of Pacifying Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 清名亞王鎮之，為士民所愛詠。

translations.literal: His reputation for purity was second only to Wang Zhenzhi's, and scholars and commoners loved to praise him in song.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for integrity was second only to Wang Zhenzhi's, and the people loved to praise him.

sentences.zh: 上表薦士曰：「臣聞陵雪褒潁，貞柯必振；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial recommending a scholar, saying: "Your servant has heard that when snow buries the high peaks of Bao and Ying, the upright branches must be shaken free;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial recommending a man of talent: "I have heard that when snow buries the peaks of Bao and Ying, the upright branches must shake free;

sentences.zh: 尊風賞流，清原斯挹。

translations.literal: when the wind of esteem honors the flowing stream, the clear source is thereby drawn upon.
translations.idiomatic: when the wind of esteem honors the flowing stream, the clear spring is drawn upon.

sentences.zh: 是以衣囊揮譽於西京，折轅延高於東帝。

translations.literal: Therefore the man with only a satchel won fame in the Western Capital, and the broken axle-shaft drew the lofty to the Eastern Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the man with only a satchel won fame in the Western Capital, and the broken carriage shaft drew the worthy to the Eastern Emperor.

sentences.zh: 伏見廣州別駕從事史朱萬嗣，年五十三，字少豫，理業沖夷，秉操純白，行稱私庭，能著官政。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed Zhu Wansi, Attending Clerk and Recorder of Guangzhou, age fifty-three, styled Shaoyu—his learning and conduct serene and plain, his integrity pure white, his private conduct praised at home, his ability notable in public office.
translations.idiomatic: I observe Zhu Wansi, attending clerk of Guangzhou, age fifty-three, courtesy name Shaoyu. His learning is profound and his conduct serene; his integrity is pure; his private life is exemplary and his public service distinguished.

sentences.zh: 雖氏非世祿，宦無通資，而隨牒南服，位極僚首，九綜州綱，三端府職，頻掌蕃機，屢績符守。

translations.literal: Although his clan did not hold hereditary stipends and he had no ready access in office, he followed his credentials to the southern regions, rose to the head of the staff, nine times grasped the province's reins, three times held key posts in the administration, frequently managed frontier affairs, and repeatedly achieved merit as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family held no hereditary rank and he had no court connections, he rose through service in the south to head the provincial staff, held nine key provincial posts and three central appointments, managed frontier affairs repeatedly, and distinguished himself as inspector more than once.

sentences.zh: 年暨知命，廉尚愈高，冰心與貪流爭激，霜情與晚節彌茂。

translations.literal: His years have reached knowing fate; his integrity rises ever higher—a heart of ice contends with the flowing greedy, frost feeling with late season grows ever fuller.
translations.idiomatic: Now past fifty, his integrity has only grown. His heart of ice stands against the tide of corruption; his frost-hardened resolve flourishes in his later years.

sentences.zh: 歷宰金山，家無寶鏤之飾；

translations.literal: Having governed Jinshan, his household had no treasure inlay ornament;
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jinshan his household held no treasure or inlay;

sentences.zh: 連組珠海，室靡璫珥之珍。

translations.literal: linked in office at Zhuhai, his rooms lacked pearl earring gems.
translations.idiomatic: as magistrate of Zhuhai his rooms held no pearl or jade ornaments.

sentences.zh: 確然守志，不求聞達，實足以澄革汙吏，洗鏡貪氓。

translations.literal: Firmly he holds his will, not seeking fame and advancement—he is truly able to clarify and reform corrupt officials and wash the mirror for greedy commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He holds firmly to his principles and seeks no advancement. He is truly fit to reform corrupt officials and shame the greedy.

sentences.zh: 臣謬忝司牧，任專萬里，雖情祗慎擢，才闕豪露，敢罄愚陋，舉其所知。

translations.literal: Your servant wrongly holds the post of provincial governor, charge extending ten thousand li; although my feeling is reverent and cautious in promotion, my talent lacks bold display—I dare exhaust my foolishness and recommend one I know.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy in my post as provincial governor, responsible for ten thousand li of territory. Though I lack the talent to display greatness, I dare offer what I know.

sentences.zh: 如得提名禮闈，抗跡朝省，摶嶺表之清風，負冰宇之潔望，則恩融一臣，而施光萬物。

translations.literal: If he could be nominated at the Rites Gate and take his place in the court and secretariat, gathering the pure wind of the Ling region and bearing the pure hope of the icy realm, then grace would melt into one minister and shine upon the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: If he could be nominated at the capital and take his place at court, bringing the pure wind of the far south and the integrity of ice to the realm, Your Majesty's grace would shine through one man upon all the world.

sentences.zh: 敢緣天澤云行，時德雨施，每甄外州，榮加遠國。

translations.literal: I dare rely on Heaven's grace moving like clouds, the age's virtue raining down, each time selecting from outer provinces and adding glory to distant states.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on Your Majesty's grace, which moves like clouds and falls like rain, honoring distant provinces and rewarding the far south.

sentences.zh: 是以獻其瞽言，希垂聽覽。」

translations.literal: Therefore I offer this blind man's words, hoping they may fall upon Your hearing."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore offer these humble words and beg that Your Majesty will hear them."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，徵以為南平王鑠冠軍司馬、長沙內史，行湘州府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Marshal of the Conquering Army under the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, Interior Secretary of Changsha, acting in the affairs of the Xiangzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was summoned to serve as marshal of the conquering army under Prince Shuo of Nanping, interior secretary of Changsha, and acting head of the Xiangzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 張尋、趙廣為亂於益州，兵寇之餘，政荒民擾。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun and Zhao Guang raised rebellion in Yizhou; after military raids and banditry, government was desolate and the people disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun and Zhao Guang rebelled in Yizhou. After years of warfare, government had collapsed and the people were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，乃追徽為持節、督益、寧二州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Hui was then recalled as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Yi and Ning provinces, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was recalled as bearer of the staff, commander of Yi and Ning military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 隱恤有方，威惠兼著，寇盜靜息，民物殷阜，蜀土安說，至今稱之。

translations.literal: He had methods for quiet succor; authority and kindness were both manifest; bandits and robbers were stilled; people and goods flourished; the land of Shu was peaceful and content—to this day he is praised.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with wise compassion; his authority and kindness were both felt; banditry ceased and prosperity returned. Shu was pacified, and he is praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died, age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 身亡之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day his person perished, the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚痛惜之，詔曰：「徽厲志廉潔，歷任恪勤，奉公盡誠，克己無倦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply grieved and cherished his memory, issuing an edict: "Hui set his will on integrity and purity; in successive posts he was reverent and diligent, serving the public with full loyalty, restraining himself without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned him deeply and issued an edict: "Hui was resolute in integrity, diligent in every post, devoted to public service, and tireless in self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 褒榮未申，不幸夙殞，言念在懷，以為傷恨。

translations.literal: Praise and glory were not yet extended; unhappily he died early; speaking of him stays in the heart, and We feel hurt and regret.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet received the honors he deserved when he died untimely. We grieve his loss.

sentences.zh: 可贈輔國將軍，本官如故。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously given General Who Assists the State, his original office unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously grant him General Who Assists the State, with his former titles confirmed.

sentences.zh: 賜錢十萬，米二百斛。

translations.literal: Grant a hundred thousand cash and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Grant a hundred thousand cash and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Viscount Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Viscount Jian.

sentences.zh: 子睿，正員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Rui was Regular Attendant Outside the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui served as regular attendant outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 弟展，臧質車騎長史、尋陽太守，質敗，從誅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhan was Chief Clerk to Zang Zhi the Cavalry General and Administrator of Xunyang; when Zhi was defeated, he was executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhan was chief clerk to Zang Zhi and administrator of Xunyang; when Zang Zhi was defeated, Zhan was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 阮長之，字茂景，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Changzhi, styled Maojing, was a man of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Changzhi, courtesy name Maojing, was from Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祖思曠，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sikuo was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ruan Sikuo was grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 父普，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Consulting Adjutant to the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ruan Pu was consulting adjutant to the general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 長之年十五喪父，有孝性，哀感傍人。

translations.literal: Changzhi at fifteen lost his father; he had a filial nature, and his grief moved those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi lost his father at fifteen. His filial grief moved all who saw him.

sentences.zh: 服除，蔬食者猶積載。

translations.literal: When mourning was over, he still ate vegetables for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he continued to eat only vegetables for years.

sentences.zh: 閒居篤學，未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Living in retirement he studied devotedly and never showed a lazy bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he studied devotedly and never showed a lazy bearing.

sentences.zh: 初為諸府參軍，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was Adjutant in various offices and was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat Outside the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as adjutant in various offices, then was appointed attendant gentleman at the secretariat outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 母老，求補襄垣令，督郵無禮，鞭之，去職。

translations.literal: His mother was old; he requested appointment as Magistrate of Xiangyuan; a postal inspector was rude, and he flogged him and left office.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was elderly, so he requested appointment as magistrate of Xiangyuan. When a postal inspector was rude to him, he had the man flogged and resigned.

sentences.zh: 尋補廬陵王義真車騎行正參軍，平越長史，東莞太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Regular Adjutant in the Cavalry Army of the Prince of Luling, Yizhen, Chief Clerk Pacifying the Yue, and Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting regular adjutant in the cavalry army of Prince Yizhen of Luling, chief clerk pacifying the Yue, and administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書殿中郎，出為武昌太守。

translations.literal: He entered office as Palace Attendant in the Secretariat and went out as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the secretariat as palace attendant and was then appointed administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時王弘為江州，雅相知重，引為車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Hong was in charge of Jiangzhou; he greatly knew and valued him and brought him in as Attending Master of Affairs in the Cavalry Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was then in charge of Jiangzhou and held him in high esteem, appointing him attending master of affairs in the cavalry army.

sentences.zh: 入為太子中舍人，中書侍郎，以母老，固辭朝直，補彭城王義康平北諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He entered as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household and Secretariat Gentleman; citing his mother's age, he firmly declined court duty and was appointed Consulting Adjutant Pacifying the North under the Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant in the heir apparent's household and secretariat gentleman. Citing his mother's age, he declined court duty and was appointed consulting adjutant pacifying the north under Prince Yikang of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，遷臨川內史，以南土卑濕，母年老，非所宜，辭不就。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Interior Secretary of Linchuan; because the southern land is low and damp and his mother was old, it was not suitable, and he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he was offered the post of interior secretary of Linchuan. He declined, saying the damp south was unsuitable for his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復除臨海太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again appointed Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 至郡少時而母亡，葬畢，不勝憂，十四年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Shortly after reaching the commandery his mother died; when the burial was complete he could not bear his grief; in the fourteenth year he died, age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he reached the commandery his mother died. When the funeral was over he could not bear his grief. In the fourteenth year he died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣田祿，芒種為斷，此前去官者，則一年秩祿皆入前人；

translations.literal: At that time prefectural and county field stipends were cut off at Grain in Ear; those who left office before this had a full year's rank salary go to the predecessor;
translations.idiomatic: At that time prefectural and county field stipends were reckoned to the Grain in Ear festival. An official who left before that date forfeited a full year's salary to his predecessor;

sentences.zh: 此後去官者，則一年秩祿皆入後人。

translations.literal: those who left after had a full year's rank salary go to the successor.
translations.idiomatic: while one who left after forfeited it to his successor.

sentences.zh: 始以元嘉末改此科，計月分祿。

translations.literal: Only at the end of Yuanjia was this rule changed, calculating salary by the month.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of the Yuanjia era was this rule changed to calculate salary by the month.

sentences.zh: 長之去武昌郡，代人未至，以芒種前一日解印綬。

translations.literal: When Changzhi left Wuchang commandery, his replacement had not yet arrived; he surrendered seal and cord the day before Grain in Ear.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhi left Wuchang, his successor had not yet arrived. He surrendered his seal and cord the day before Grain in Ear.

sentences.zh: 初發京師，親故或以器物贈別，得便緘錄，後歸，悉以還之。

translations.literal: When he first set out from the capital, relatives and friends sometimes gave parting gifts of objects; he sealed and recorded them when convenient, and on returning later returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: When he first left the capital, relatives and friends gave him parting gifts. He sealed and recorded each item and returned them all on his return.

sentences.zh: 在中書省直，夜往鄰省，誤著履出閣，依事自列門下；

translations.literal: While on duty at the Secretariat, at night he went to a neighboring office, mistakenly wearing his shoes out through the gate; according to regulation he reported himself to the Gate Department;
translations.idiomatic: While on secretariat duty he went one night to a neighboring office and accidentally walked out through the gate still wearing his shoes. He reported himself to the gate department as required;

sentences.zh: 門下以闇夜人不知，不受列。

translations.literal: the Gate Department, because it was dark night and no one knew, did not accept his report.
translations.idiomatic: but the gate department, saying no one had seen him in the dark, refused to take the report.

sentences.zh: 長之固遣送之，曰：「一生不侮闇室。」

translations.literal: Changzhi firmly sent it in anyway, saying: "In a lifetime one does not cheat a dark room.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi insisted on submitting it anyway, saying: "A man does not deceive even an empty room in the dark.

sentences.zh: 前後所蒞官，皆有風政，為後人所思。

translations.literal: In every office he held before and after there was exemplary governance, and later people remember him.
translations.idiomatic: Every office he held was marked by exemplary governance, and later generations remember him.

sentences.zh: 宋世言善治者，咸稱之。

translations.literal: In the Song age, when speaking of those who governed well, all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song dynasty, whenever good governance was discussed, his name was always mentioned.

sentences.zh: 子師門，原鄉令。

translations.literal: His son Shimmen was Magistrate of Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shimmen was magistrate of Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉在臨海，並以簡約見稱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Linhai; in both posts he was praised for simplicity and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Linhai; in both posts he was praised for simplicity and austerity.

sentences.zh: 所得祿秩，悉散之親故，妻子常饑寒。

translations.literal: All salary and rank income he gave away to relatives and friends; wife and children were often hungry and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all his salary to relatives and friends; his wife and children often went hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 人有勸其營田者，秉之正色曰：「食祿之家，豈可與農人競利！」

translations.literal: When someone urged him to cultivate fields, Bingzhi said sternly: "A household that lives on stipends—how can it compete for profit with farmers!
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to cultivate fields, Bingzhi said sternly: "A household that lives on official salary—how can it compete with farmers for profit!

sentences.zh: 在郡作書案一枚，及去官，留以付庫。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had one writing desk made; when he left office he left it to be handed to the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he had one writing desk made; when he left office he left it for the government storehouse.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died, age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子徽，尚書都官郎，吳令。

translations.literal: His son Hui was Gentleman of the Punishments Section in the Secretariat and Magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui served as gentleman of the punishments section and magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 元兇殺徐湛之，徽以黨與見誅。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as his accomplice.

sentences.zh: 子謐，昇明末為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: His son Mi at the end of the Shengping era was Gentleman of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi served as gentleman of the personnel section at the end of the Shengping era.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，太祖遣大使巡行四方，兼散騎常侍孔默之、王歆之等上言：「宣威將軍、陳、南頓二郡太守李元德，清勤均平，姦盜止息。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia the Founder Emperor sent great envoys to tour the four quarters; Attendant Cavalier Regular Kong Mozhi, Wang Xinzhi, and others memorialized: "General Who Proclaims Might, Administrator of Chen and Nandun commanderies Li Yuande is pure, diligent, fair, and even; treachery and theft have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen sent envoys to tour the realm. Attendant cavalier regular Kong Mozhi, Wang Xinzhi, and others reported: "General Who Proclaims Might Li Yuande, administrator of Chen and Nandun, is diligent, fair, and incorrupt; crime has ceased in his districts.

sentences.zh: 彭城內史魏恭子，廉恪脩慎，在公忘私，安約守儉，久而彌固。

translations.literal: Interior Secretary of Pengcheng Wei Gongzi is pure, reverent, cultivated, and cautious, in public forgetting private interest, content in simplicity and holding to frugality, which over time grows ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gongzi, interior secretary of Pengcheng, is pure, cautious, and self-restrained, devoted to public duty and frugal in his habits, virtues that have only grown firmer with time.

sentences.zh: 前宋縣令成浦，治政寬濟，遺詠在民。

translations.literal: Former Magistrate of Song Cheng Pu governed with leniency and relief; songs of praise he left remain among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Former magistrate of Song Cheng Pu governed with leniency and compassion, and the people still sing his praise.

sentences.zh: 前鮦陽令李熙國，在事有方，民思其政。

translations.literal: Former Magistrate of Tiaoyang Li Xiguo had methods in office; the people miss his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Former magistrate of Tiaoyang Li Xiguo governed effectively, and the people still miss him.

sentences.zh: 山桑令何道，自少清廉，白首彌厲。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shansang He Dao has been pure from youth, and to white-haired age grows ever stricter.
translations.idiomatic: He Dao, magistrate of Shansang, has been incorrupt since youth and grows only stricter in old age.

sentences.zh: 應加褒齎，以勸於後。」

translations.literal: They should receive added praise and reward to encourage those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: They deserve reward to encourage others to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 乃進元德號寧朔將軍，恭子賜絹五十匹，穀五百斛；

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuande's title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North; Gongzi was granted fifty bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Yuande was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North; Gongzi received fifty bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain;

sentences.zh: 浦、熙國、道各賜絹三十匹，穀二百斛。

translations.literal: Pu, Xiguo, and Dao were each granted thirty bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, Xiguo, and Dao each received thirty bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 王歆之，字叔道，河東人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xinzhi, styled Shudao, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xinzhi, courtesy name Shudao, was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖愆期，有名晉世，官至南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qianqi was famous in the Jin age and reached the post of Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qianqi was renowned in the Jin dynasty and rose to colonel of the southern Man.

sentences.zh: 祖尋之，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xunzhi was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Xunzhi was grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 父肇之，豫章公相。

translations.literal: His father Zhaozhi was Chancellor to the Duke of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zhaozhi was chancellor to the Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歆之被遇於太祖，歷顯官左民尚書，光祿大夫，卒官。

translations.literal: Xinzhi received favor from Emperor Wen, passed through eminent offices as Minister of the Left for the People and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi won favor from Emperor Wen, served as minister of the left for the people and grand master for splendid happiness, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，豫州刺史長沙王義欣上言：「所統威遠將軍、北譙梁二郡太守關中侯申季歷，自奉職邦畿，於茲五年，信惠並宣，威化兼著，外清姦暴，內輯民黎，役賦均平，閭井齊肅，綏穆初附，招攜荒遠，郊境之外，仰澤懷風，爵賞之授，績能是顯，宜升階秩，以崇獎勸。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Changsha Yixin, memorialized: "Under my command General Who Establishes Distance, Administrator of Bei and Qiao and Liang commanderies, Marquis within the Passes Shen Jili, since taking office in the capital region, for five years now, trust and kindness have both been proclaimed, authority and transformation both manifest; without he has cleared treachery and violence, within he has settled the people; corvée and levies are fair and even, lanes and wells are all orderly; he has pacified those newly attached and drawn in the remote and wild; beyond the suburbs they look up to his grace and cherish his wind; in granting titles and rewards, merit and ability are thereby displayed—he should be advanced in rank to honor and encourage."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Prince Yixin of Changsha, inspector of Yuzhou, reported: "General Who Establishes Distance Shen Jili, marquis within the passes and administrator of Bei, Qiao, and Liang, has served in the capital region for five years. His trustworthiness and kindness are felt throughout his districts; he has suppressed violence abroad and brought order at home; levies are fair and the people live in peace. He has pacified newly submitted peoples and drawn in the remote frontier. Beyond the suburbs the people look to his grace. His merit warrants promotion in rank as encouragement to others."

sentences.zh: 進號寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 其後晉壽太守郭啟玄亦有清節，卒官。

translations.literal: Later Guo Qixuan, Administrator of Jinshou, also had a pure integrity and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Qixuan, administrator of Jinshou, was also known for integrity and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，詔曰：「故綏遠將軍、晉壽太守郭啟玄往銜命虜庭，秉意不屈，受任白水，盡勤靡懈，公奉私餼，纖毫弗納，布衣蔬食，飭躬惟儉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia an edict said: "The late General of Pacifying Distance, Administrator of Jinshou Guo Qixuan formerly bore orders in the barbarian court, holding his will unbent; receiving appointment at Baishui, he was fully diligent without slackening; public offerings and private gifts he accepted not the slightest; plain cloth and vegetable food, restraining his person in frugality alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia an edict declared: "The late General of Pacifying Distance Guo Qixuan, former administrator of Jinshou, once bore imperial orders in the northern court and would not bend his will. At Baishui he served tirelessly, accepting neither public offerings nor private gifts, living on plain cloth and vegetables in austere self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 故超授顯邦，以甄廉績。

translations.literal: Therefore he was exceptionally given a prominent commandery to display his pure achievements.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore appointed him to a prominent commandery to honor his integrity.

sentences.zh: 而介誠苦節，終始匪貳，身死之日，妻子凍餒，志操殊俗，良可哀悼。

translations.literal: Yet his upright sincerity and bitter integrity from beginning to end were not double; on the day his person died, wife and children were frozen and starving—his will and conduct unlike the common, truly worthy of mourning.
