translations.idiomatic: His integrity never wavered from first to last. When he died his wife and children were left hungry and cold. His conduct was unlike ordinary men, and We deeply mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可賜其家穀五百斛。」

translations.literal: His household may be granted five hundred hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Grant his household five hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 時有北地傅僧祐、潁川陳瑉、高平張祐，並以吏才見知。

translations.literal: At the time there were Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping, all known for talent in administration.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping were all known for administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 僧祐事在《臧燾傳》。

translations.literal: Sengyou's affairs are in the biography of Zang Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou's career is treated in the biography of Zang Tao.

sentences.zh: 瑉為吳令，善發姦伏，境內以為神明。

translations.literal: Min was Magistrate of Wu, skilled at exposing hidden wrongdoing; within the borders he was regarded as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min served as magistrate of Wu and excelled at uncovering hidden crimes; the people regarded him as almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 祐祖父湛，晉孝武世，以才學為中書侍郎，光祿勳。

translations.literal: You's grandfather Zhan, in the age of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, by talent and learning was Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Minister of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You's grandfather Zhang Zhan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, rose by learning to secretariat gentleman and grand minister of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 祐歷臨安、武康、錢塘令，並著能名，宋世言長吏者，以三人為首。

translations.literal: You successively held the magistracies of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang, in all gaining a name for ability; when the Song age spoke of chief magistrates, these three men were placed first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You served as magistrate of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang in turn, earning a reputation for ability in each. In the Song dynasty these three were ranked foremost among district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，高平太守潘詞，有清節。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia, Pan Ci, Administrator of Gaoping, had pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia era Pan Ci, administrator of Gaoping, was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 子亮為昌慮令，亦著廉名，大明中，為徐州刺史劉道隆所表。

translations.literal: His son Liang was Magistrate of Changlu and also had a name for purity; in Daming he was recommended by Liu Daolong, Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang served as magistrate of Changlu and was also known for integrity; in the Daming era he was recommended by Liu Daolong, inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，吳郡陸法真歷官有清節，嘗為劉秀之安北錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Xiaowu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery in successive offices had pure integrity and once was Recorder of Liu Xiuzhi's Army Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery held several posts marked by integrity and once served as recorder on Liu Xiuzhi's staff as army pacifying the north.

sentences.zh: 泰山羊希與安北諮議參軍孫詵書曰：「足下同僚似有陸錄事者，此生東南名地，又張玄外孫，持身至清，雅有志節。

translations.literal: Yang Xi of Taishan wrote to Sun Shen, Consulting Adjutant Pacifying the North: "Among your colleagues below there seems to be Recorder Lu; this man's family is a famous house of the southeast, and he is also the maternal grandson of Zhang Xuan—he holds himself in utmost purity and has lofty will and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi of Taishan wrote to Sun Shen, consulting adjutant pacifying the north: "Among your colleagues there seems to be a Recorder Lu. He comes from a distinguished southeastern family and is the maternal grandson of Zhang Xuan. He is utterly incorrupt and has lofty principles.

sentences.zh: 年高官下，秉操不衰，計當日夕相與申意。」

translations.literal: His years are high yet his office low; he holds his conduct undiminished—I expect we shall before long share our feelings with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years he holds a humble post, yet his integrity has not faded. I expect we shall speak together soon.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為南海太守，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was Administrator of Nanhai and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was appointed administrator of Nanhai and died in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，琅邪王悅，亦蒞官清正見知。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Ming, Wang Yue of Langye was also known for holding office in purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming, Wang Yue of Langye was also known for incorrupt service.

sentences.zh: 悅字少明，晉右將軍羲之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Shaoming, was a great-great-grandson of Xi Zhi, Right General of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, courtesy name Shaoming, was a great-great-grandson of the Jin calligrapher Wang Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 父靖之，官至司徒左長史。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi reached the post of Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Jingzhi rose to left chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 靖之為劉穆之所厚，就穆之求侍中，如此非一。

translations.literal: Jingzhi was favored by Liu Muzhi and went to Muzhi to request the post of Palace Attendant—not once only.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi was favored by Liu Muzhi and repeatedly asked him for the post of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「卿若不求，久自得也。」

translations.literal: Muzhi said: "If you did not ask, in time you would obtain it of yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said: "If you had not asked, you would have received it in time on your own.

sentences.zh: 遂不果。

translations.literal: In the end it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never received it.

sentences.zh: 悅泰始中，為黃門郎，御史中丞。

translations.literal: Yue in the Taishi era was Yellow Gate Gentleman and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taishi reign Yue served as yellow gate gentleman and imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 上以其廉介，賜良田五頃。

translations.literal: The emperor because of his purity and integrity granted him five qing of good farmland.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him five qing of good farmland for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，侍中，在門下，盡其心力。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat and Palace Attendant; in the Gate Department he exhausted his heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman of the personnel section and palace attendant, serving in the gate department with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒官，追贈太常。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office; posthumously he was given the Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，悅為侍中，檢校御府、太官、太醫諸署，得姦巧甚多。

translations.literal: At first, when Yue was Palace Attendant, he inspected and checked the Imperial Storehouse, Grand Provisioner, Imperial Physicians, and other offices, uncovering a great deal of fraud and trickery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue served as palace attendant he inspected the imperial storehouse, grand provisioner, imperial physicians, and other offices, uncovering extensive fraud.

sentences.zh: 及悅死，眾咸謂諸署詋詛之，上乃收典掌者十餘人，桎梏云送淮陰，密令渡瓜步江，投之中流。

translations.literal: When Yue died, the multitude all said the offices had cursed him; the emperor then arrested more than ten men in charge, put them in cangue and fetters saying they were sent to Huaiyin, secretly ordered them ferried across the Guabu River, and cast them into midstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue died, many believed the offices had cursed him. The emperor arrested more than ten officials in charge, claiming they were being sent to Huaiyin, then secretly had them ferried across the Guabu River and thrown into midstream.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫善政之於民，猶良工之於埴也，用功寡而成器多。

translations.literal: The historian says: Good government toward the people is like a skilled craftsman toward clay—little effort applied, yet many vessels formed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Good government toward the people is like a skilled potter with clay: little effort yields many vessels.

sentences.zh: 漢世戶口殷盛，刑務簡闊，郡縣治民，無所橫擾，勸賞威刑，事多專斷，尺一詔書，希經邦邑，龔、黃之化，易以有成。

translations.literal: In the Han age households were abundant and flourishing, penal affairs simple and broad; prefectures and counties governed the people without arbitrary harassment; encouragement, reward, authority, and punishment were mostly decided on their own authority; imperial edicts a foot long rarely passed through the state and towns—the transformation of Gong and Huang was easy to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the population was large, the law simple, and local officials governed without arbitrary interference. Magistrates had wide discretion in rewards and punishments, and imperial edicts rarely reached every district. The gentle governance of Gong Yu and Huang Ba was easy to achieve.

sentences.zh: 降及晚代，情偽繁起，民減昔時，務多前世，立績垂風，艱易百倍。

translations.literal: Descending to the late age, feeling and falsity arose in profusion; the people were fewer than in former times, affairs more numerous than in earlier generations; to establish merit and leave a wind behind was a hundred times harder than easy.
translations.idiomatic: By later ages deceit had multiplied, the population had shrunk, and official burdens had grown. To achieve lasting good governance was a hundred times harder.

sentences.zh: 若以上古之化，治此世之民，今吏之良，撫前代之俗，則武城弦歌，將有未暇；

translations.literal: If with the transformation of high antiquity one governed the people of this age, or if the good officials of today soothed the customs of former generations, then the zither songs of Wucheng would have no leisure;
translations.idiomatic: If the governance of antiquity were applied to the people of this age, or if today's good officials were set to govern the customs of earlier times, then the zither songs of Wucheng would have no time to sound;

sentences.zh: 淮陽臥治，如或可勉。

translations.literal: the recumbent governance of Huaiyang might perhaps be striven for.
translations.idiomatic: the recumbent governance of Huaiyang might perhaps still be within reach.

sentences.zh: 未必今才陋古，蓋化有淳薄也。

translations.literal: It is not necessarily that today's talent is base compared with antiquity—rather, transformation has its pure and its thin.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that talent today is inferior to that of antiquity; rather, the age itself has grown coarse.
